verdict: Marathon Petroleum had a windfall quarter: refining margins nearly tripled to $45.70 a barrel, its refineries ran flat-out, and net income quintupled to $7.4B.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +58% YoY on high prices and volumes

kpis.label: Refining margin
kpis.note: vs $17.60 a year ago — the whole story

segments.name: Sales & other operating revenues
segments.note: Selling gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and other products from the largest U.S. refining system — 3.2 million barrels a day of throughput at 100% utilization, at much higher prices.

segments.name: Income from equity investments
segments.note: Marathon's share of profit from ventures it part-owns — down from $976M a year ago, when it included larger midstream-related gains.

opex.note: Running the refining, marketing and corporate organization.

opex.note: Wearing-out cost of refineries, pipelines and terminals.

otherDetail: Net interest and other financial costs of $287M.

takeaways.title: Crack spreads exploded
takeaways.text: The refining margin — what a barrel of crude becomes worth as fuel — hit $45.70 per barrel versus $17.60 a year ago, on strong demand and tight supply. Refining & Marketing EBITDA rose to $9.9B from $1.8B.

takeaways.title: Refineries ran flat-out
takeaways.text: Crude capacity utilization was 100% (from 95%), with 3.2 million barrels a day of throughput — the system caught the margin wave at full volume.

takeaways.title: A market windfall, not a one-off
takeaways.text: Adjusted net income ($7.5B) was barely above GAAP ($7.4B): there was no big asset-sale gain to strip out. The profit came from the market — which also means it can reverse when spreads normalize.

footerNote: Marathon does not break revenue out by segment in its release (segments are reported as adjusted EBITDA: Refining & Marketing $9,895M, Midstream $1,882M, Renewable Diesel $254M), so the chart's sources are its reported revenue lines. Net income attributable to MPC was $7,447M; consolidated net income was $7,878M, with $431M attributable to noncontrolling interests (mainly public holders of MPLX).
